questions.q: When checking the finished design against Lesson 36's scope, what determines whether the capstone is actually done?
options: Every promised row in the scope table has a real answer, and the design does exactly what was scoped — not because it has extra unrequested features
Whether the design has more tables than the scope originally listed
Whether the fact table has at least ten measures
Whether the design was finished faster than Lesson 36 estimated
questions.explain: The wrap-up check is about matching the original scope precisely, the same way SSIS Development's and SSRS Development's capstones checked their finished projects against their own scope tables.

questions.q: In the recommended presentation order for this project, what should be shown first?
options: The grain and the dimension list, explaining the SCD type behind each dimension
The indexing and partitioning statements
The clustered columnstore index syntax
The partition function values
questions.explain: Starting with the grain and dimensions, then the fact table, then indexing/partitioning last, walks a listener through the design in the same order it was actually made — from business meaning down to physical performance.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say explaining the accumulating snapshot classification is a 'fair proxy' for real understanding in an interview?
options: Because getting the fact table type right requires actually understanding how the business process behaves over time, not just knowing CREATE TABLE syntax
Because accumulating snapshot is the only fact table type that exists
Because interviewers only ever ask about indexing
Because the classification has no real design consequence
questions.explain: Choosing the right fact table type depends on understanding the business process's actual lifecycle — a much better signal of design understanding than syntax knowledge alone.

questions.q: According to the resume language example in this lesson, which SCD strategy pattern does the finished design use across its dimensions?
options: A mix of Type 0, Type 1, and Type 2 strategies, chosen per dimension based on whether that dimension's attributes need history tracked
Every dimension uses Type 2
Every dimension uses Type 0
SCD types were not considered in this design
questions.explain: DimShipMethod is Type 0, DimProduct and DimEmployee are Type 1, and DimVendor is Type 2 — the resume language deliberately reflects that mixed, deliberate set of choices.

questions.q: What is the next course in this catalog after Data Modeling & Data Warehousing, and what does it add?
options: Microsoft Data & BI Capstone + Job Preparation — folding this project into a full portfolio alongside T-SQL, SSIS, SSRS, and Power BI work, plus resume and interview preparation
Data Modeling & Data Warehousing repeats itself with new content
A course on Oracle Financial Applications
There is no next course in this catalog
questions.explain: Per this catalog's course list, Microsoft Data & BI Capstone + Job Preparation is the course that follows, and it's specifically built to combine this course's warehouse design work with the rest of the SQL Server BI stack for job readiness.
